items.title: The Serre tensor ideal cut out by a homological functor, and the localisation diagram it produces
items.author: Paul Balmer
items.work: Homological support of big objects in tensor-triangulated categories
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 7 (2020), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.135
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma works with a big tensor-triangulated category mT satisfying the standing hypothesis and a Serre tensor ideal cC, and claims that the full subcategory cB of objects whose image under hat F lies in cC is a maximal Serre tensor ideal, that a four-square diagram of localisations and adjoints commutes in the four stated ways, and that the pure-injective object EB is a direct summand of U(EC) (statement lines 765-785). The proof applies the homological-functor criterion to the composite H = Q_cC o hat F o yoneda_T, factors it through the localisation at cB, and then compares the two right adjoints of the same functor to obtain R_cB o bar U = hat U o R_cC (proof lines 795-813). The step that carries the content is that comparison of right adjoints: it is what transfers the injective-hull decomposition from the localised category AB to the original category cT, and the author explicitly notes that the decomposition already holds in cT by a cited clause. The argument uses Grothendieck-category theory in the form of a right-adjoint existence statement rather than a computation. H2.
